facts.fact: KRAY 连续四天的上午和下午都在总部星巴克寻找 BUTTONFLY。
facts.anchor: Over the next four days KRAY looked for BUTTONFLY every morning and afternoon down at the Headquarters Starbucks.

facts.fact: 周五 4 月 16 日下午 4 点 30 分，KRAY 终于在靠后的桌边看到他正和一名年轻案件官交谈。
facts.anchor: Finally, at 4:30 p.m. on Friday, April 16, KRAY spotted him sitting at a table in the back talking with a young case officer.

facts.fact: KRAY 说 Wacker 把他安置在“惩罚区”，还把他转介给反间谍组。
facts.anchor: But now they have me sitting in the Penalty Box. And Wacker has referred me to the Counterespionage Group.

facts.fact: BUTTONFLY 说反间谍组虽然没几个正经人，却把自己看得很严肃；查不出问题就会捏造。
facts.anchor: Even though there are no serious people working there, CEG takes itself very seriously. If they can’t find anything, they’ll fudge it.

facts.fact: Wacker 指责 KRAY 与 KANDINSKY 的关系，并怪他没有上报那名在印度主动搭话约两分钟的陌生人。
facts.anchor: He says he doesn’t like my relationship with KANDINSKY. He says I should have reported some guy in India who walked up and talked to me for two minutes.

facts.fact: BUTTONFLY 说自己本科和法学院都在耶鲁，成绩是清一色的 C。
facts.anchor: “Yep. Undergraduate too. Double-barreled. Solid Cs, by the way.”

facts.fact: BUTTONFLY 把嘴张成圆形，又用指节敲头顶，发出阴沉的回声。
facts.anchor: Then he opened his mouth, forming it into a circle. He rapped on the top of his skull with his knuckles, producing a lugubrious echo.

facts.fact: BUTTONFLY 说局里不少掌权者都待过“惩罚区”，后来照样恢复了势头。
facts.anchor: Plenty of people running the Agency have spent time in the Penalty Box and recovered their momentum afterward.
